<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Isaía Prophéta
<r>Isa 66:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Hæc dicit Dóminus: Cælum sedes mea, terra autem scabéllum pedum meórum. Quæ est ista domus quam ædificábitis mihi? et quis est iste locus quiétis meæ?
<n>2</n> Omnia hæc manus mea fecit, et facta sunt univérsa ista, dicit Dóminus: ad quem autem respíciam, nisi ad paupérculum, et contrítum spíritu, et treméntem sermónes meos?
<n>3</n> Qui ímmolat bovem, quasi qui interfíciat virum.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Cánite tuba in Sion, vocáte gentes, annuntiáte pópulis, et dícite:

<r>℟.</r> Ecce Deus Salvátor noster advéniet.

b.51095a293c:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>N</c>ono Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna vicésima sexta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>V</h>igília Nativitátis Dómini nostri Iesu Christi.
<h>C</h>racóviæ, in Polónia, natális sancti Ioánnis Cántii, Presbýteri et Confessóris, quem, doctrína, propagándæ fídei zelo, virtútibus ac miráculis clarum, Clemens Décimus tértius, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum número adscrípsit. Eius autem festívitas tertiodécimo Kaléndas Novémbris celebrátur.
<h>A</h>pud Spolétum sancti Gregórii, Presbýteri et Mártyris; qui, tempóribus Diocletiáni et Maximiáni Imperatórum, primo nodósis fústibus cæsus, ac deínde, post cratículam et cárcerem, cárduis férreis in génibus percússus, sed et ardéntibus lampádibus per látera incénsus, tandem est decollátus.
<h>T</h>rípoli, in Phœnícia, sanctórum Mártyrum Luciáni, Metróbii, Pauli, Zenóbii, Theotími et Drusi.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ sancti Euthýmii Mártyris, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, cum multos ad martýrium præmisísset, et ipse, ense transfíxus, eos secútus est ad corónam.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ natális sanctárum Vírginum quadragínta, quæ, in Deciána persecutióne, per divérsa torménta martýrium consummárunt.
<h>B</h>urdígalæ sancti Delphíni Epíscopi, qui, Theodósii témpore, cláruit sanctitáte.
<h>R</h>omæ natális sanctæ Tharsíllæ Vírginis, ámitæ sancti Gregórii Papæ, de qua ipse testátur quod in hora éxitus sui Iesum ad se veniéntem víderit.
<h>T</h>réviris sanctæ Irminæ Vírginis, fíliæ Dagobérti Regis.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.b3b694fc62:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 24th 2027, the 26th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>he morrow is the Eve of the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ.
<h>U</h>pon the same 24th day of December, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Cracow, in Poland, (in the year 1473,) holy John of Kenty, Priest and Confessor, famous for his learning, his zeal for the spreading of the faith, his graces, and his miracles, whose name Pope Clement XIII enrolled among those of the Saints. His feast, however, is kept upon the 20th day of October.
<h>A</h>t Spoleto, the holy Priest Gregory (of Spoleto), a martyr in the time of the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, he was beaten with knotted cudgels, laid upon a grating over fire, imprisoned, his knees hammered with iron combs, burning lamps set to his sides, and at last beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Tripoli, the holy martyrs Lucian, Metrobius, Paul, Zenobius, Theotimus, and Drusus.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the holy martyr Euthymius, who sent many before him to martyrdom, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian, and then was himself pierced through with the sword, and so followed them unto their crown.
<h>A</h>t Antioch, forty holy Virgins and martyrs, who there finished their testimony by diverse torments in the persecution under the Emperor Decius.
<h>A</h>t Bordeaux, holy Delphinus, Bishop (of that see from 380-404, when he died,) who was a burning and shining light of holiness in the time of the Emperor Theodosius.
<h>A</h>t Rome, (about the year 550,) the holy Virgin Tharsilla, father's sister to holy Pope Gregory, of whom he witnesseth that at the hour of her going forth she saw Jesus coming unto her.
<h>A</h>t Trier, the holy Virgin Irmina, daughter to King Dagobert (II. She was Abbess of the monastery of Horrein, and lived from about the year 672 to about the year 715.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
